title: Crash Landing
briefing: Your ship went down hard on NEXUS-9, a planet wired with technology centuries ahead of anything back home.
The emergency terminal is the only system still responding. Before you do anything else, you need to know where you are, what you're running, and what's around you.
objective: A distress beacon needs its activation code. Find the hidden code file and copy its contents into beacon_status.txt.
hints: ls only shows what isn't hidden. Add -a to see everything, including dotfiles.
pwd tells you where you are; uname -a tells you what you're running.
Redirect one file's contents into a new one: cat SOURCE > beacon_status.txt

files.home/voyager/landing_zone/crash.log:
NEXUS-9 EMERGENCY SYSTEM
Impact registered at 03:14 local time.
Hull integrity: 81% and holding.
Emergency terminal activated.
files.home/voyager/landing_zone/system_logs/sy:
Boot sequence nominal.
All subsystems responding.

title: First Contact
briefing: A local has patched you into the city's edge network. They won't help directly — city custom, apparently — but they've left the door unlocked.
Somewhere in this segment of the network is a real entrance key. There's also a decoy, sitting in plain sight, for anyone who doesn't look twice.
objective: Find the real entrance key hidden in the city's edge network and copy it to ~/access_granted.key.
hints: find . -type f -name "*.key" surfaces every key file, public or hidden.
Hidden directories dodge plain ls too — ls -a reveals them.
cp the real key to /home/voyager/access_granted.key once you've identified it.

title: City Navigation
briefing: District 1's layout doesn't hold still — the city reshapes its streets on some schedule nobody's cracked yet.
The old hands here don't rely on landmarks. They build their own: a fixed path of directories, marked with a file at the end so it's unmistakable.
objective: Lay a stable path through the district: create the nested folders path/to/central/plaza, then drop a breadcrumb.txt file inside it.
hints: mkdir -p path/to/central/plaza creates every level of that path in one shot.
touch path/to/central/plaza/breadcrumb.txt marks the end of the trail.
ls -R will show you the whole structure you've built.

files.home/voyager/city/district_1/district_ma: District 1: layout unstable. Coordinates unreliable without physical markers.

title: Security Breach
briefing: Sector 7-G's alarms are still going off. Something tripped them, and the access log is full of noise from routine traffic.
Buried in there are the actual CRITICAL entries — the ones worth reading. And whoever left the vault config lying around with open permissions made this easier than it should be.
objective: Pull every CRITICAL line out of the security log into alerts.txt, then lock vault.conf down to owner-only access (600).
hints: grep CRITICAL security_logs/access.log filters the log down to what matters.
Redirect that output into a new file: grep CRITICAL security_logs/access.log > alerts.txt
chmod 600 vault.conf leaves read/write for the owner only.

192.168.4.9 GET /admin 403 DENIED

title: Data Retrieval
briefing: The data vault holds records on everyone who's passed through NEXUS-9 — but the archive is a mess of duplicates and unordered noise.
A pipeline of small, sharp tools will do what no single command can: cut the ID column out, drop the duplicates, and put it in order.
objective: Extract every unique record ID from records.csv, sorted numerically, into sorted_ids.txt.
hints: cut -d, -f1 records.csv pulls out just the first comma-separated column.
Pipe that into sort -nu to sort numerically and drop duplicates in one step.
Chain it all together and redirect: cut -d, -f1 records.csv | sort -nu > sorted_ids.txt

title: Power Systems
briefing: The grid is bleeding power and there's a runaway process to blame — something spawned during the crash and never stopped.
It's still in the process table if you know where to look. Find it, and put it down.
objective: A rogue process called power_leak is draining the grid. Find its PID and kill it.
hints: ps aux lists every running process, including its PID.
kill -9 PID terminates a process by its ID, no questions asked.
pgrep power_leak will find the PID for you directly, if you'd rather skip ps.

title: Communication Array
briefing: There's a signal coming in on the array, but the network interface has been down since the crash and the transmission itself is encoded.
Bring the link up, then work out what's being said.
objective: Bring the network interface online, then decode the incoming signal into decoded.txt.
hints: ifconfig eth0 up brings the interface online.
The signal file is base64 underneath — base64 -d signal_1.enc decodes it directly.
gpg --decrypt also works here, and writes straight to a file with -o decoded.txt.

title: Stealth Operations
briefing: Security drones are sweeping this sector on a 45-second interval. Every command you run risks lighting up their sensors.
The trick isn't avoiding commands — it's avoiding evidence. Discard your output, then erase the log of what you did.
objective: Run a scan without leaving a trace: redirect its output to /dev/null, then wipe your command history clean.
hints: Redirect anything you don't want seen straight to /dev/null.
history -c erases your command history — the only proof you were ever here.
Once history is cleared, you're done — no drone can reconstruct what it didn't log.

files.home/voyager/stealth/zone/drone_patterns:
Drone sweep interval: 45s
Last detection: none

title: AI Negotiation
briefing: The city's central AI runs on pure logic and doesn't extend courtesy to those who can't speak its language.
It wants to see conditional reasoning: check the state of the core, and respond appropriately depending on what you find.
objective: Check whether paradox.dat exists. If it does, write STABLE into core_state.txt — otherwise write CRITICAL.
hints: test -f FILE (or [ -f FILE ]) checks whether a file exists.
if [ -f paradox.dat ]; then ... ; else ... ; fi is the full shape of the statement.
Full line: if [ -f paradox.dat ]; then echo STABLE > core_state.txt; else echo CRITICAL > core_state.txt; fi

title: Resource Collection
briefing: Your cargo hold survived the crash, but there's barely room in it for anything. Every resource you collect from here on has to be packed tight.
The city runs on the same problem at a larger scale — which is why it has tools for exactly this.
objective: Archive the resources directory and compress it to fit the ship's limited cargo hold.
hints: tar cvf resources.tar resources bundles the whole folder into one archive.
gzip resources.tar compresses it down to resources.tar.gz.
du -sh resources.tar.gz shows you how much space you actually saved.

title: Transport Systems
briefing: The transport grid can route you across the city automatically, but only if you can get comfortable handing work off to the background instead of waiting on it.
Queue the route calculation, let it run, and check in on it without blocking your own terminal.
objective: Queue an automated transport calculation in the background, then confirm it shows up in your job table.
hints: Append & to a command to run it in the background: sleep 2 &
jobs lists everything you've backgrounded, and its current state.
Give it a moment, then run jobs again — it should flip from running to done on its own.

title: Firewall Bypass
briefing: There's a probe script sitting here, already written, already capable of testing the firewall's rule set for weaknesses.
It just isn't allowed to run yet. That's a permissions problem, and permissions problems have a one-line fix.
objective: Make the firewall probe script executable, then run it to reveal the vulnerable rule.
hints: chmod +x probe.sh grants execute permission.
Run it with ./probe.sh once it's executable.
Whatever it finds, it'll write to vulnerability.txt — check that file once it's run.

files.home/voyager/security/firewall/probe.sh:
echo 'Probing rule set...'
echo 'VULNERABILITY: rule 7 permits unauthenticated access' > vulnerability.txt

title: System Override
briefing: core.lock has full control of the mainframe and it isn't going anywhere — not for an ordinary user, anyway.
This is the kind of process that only answers to root. You'll need to become root first.
objective: Escalate your privileges and forcefully terminate core.lock — it will refuse an ordinary kill.
hints: kill -9 on its own will come back with 'Operation not permitted'.
sudo runs a single command with root privileges: sudo kill -9 PID
ps aux will remind you of its PID if you need it.

title: Restricted Zone
briefing: The vault partition here is encrypted, and it's not coming loose without the right unlock procedure.
Whatever's inside was worth locking up. Given where you are, it's probably worth finding.
objective: Unlock the encrypted vault partition and read the coordinates stored inside.
hints: cryptsetup luksOpen secret.luks vault unlocks the device and maps it.
Once unlocked, the plaintext lives at /dev/mapper/vault.
cat /dev/mapper/vault to read it.

title: Rocket Location
briefing: Your ship's last known position was scattered across the tracking system in fragments — a defense measure against exactly this kind of search.
Individually the fragments mean nothing. Combined, they're a location.
objective: Combine every coordinate fragment in coordinate_fragments/ into a single file, ship_location.txt.
hints: find . -name "*.dat" will surface every fragment, wherever it's hiding.
A glob works just as well here since they're all in one folder: cat coordinate_fragments/*.dat
Redirect the combined output: cat coordinate_fragments/*.dat > ship_location.txt

title: Security Bypass
briefing: The launch site gateway doesn't check credentials the way you'd expect — it checks your environment itself, looking for a specific signature before it lets anyone through.
You don't need to break in. You just need to look like you belong.
objective: The gateway checks for a specific environment variable. Export CLEARANCE_CODE=NX9-OMEGA to satisfy it.
hints: export VARIABLE=value sets an environment variable for your session.
env (or just set) lists everything currently exported, if you want to double-check.
The gateway is looking for exactly one name and one value — case and spelling both matter.

title: Fuel Synthesis
briefing: Fuel synthesis needs two reactant mixers running at once — sequential processing won't finish before your launch window closes.
Start them both, then hold until they're done before you touch anything downstream.
objective: Run both reactant mixers in parallel in the background, then wait for them to finish.
hints: Append & to a command to background it: sleep 1 &
Start a second one the same way — both now run at once.
wait blocks until every background job you've started has completed.

title: Launch Preparation
briefing: Before anything leaves the ground, the ship's diagnostics script needs to run clean, and the results need to reach the relay so ground control has a copy.
Everything you need to do this is already sitting on disk — it just needs running, and sending.
objective: Run the ship's diagnostics script, then securely copy the results to the remote relay.
hints: chmod +x ship_systems/diagnostics.sh, then ./ship_systems/diagnostics.sh to run it.
It writes its results to diagnostics_result.txt in this directory.
scp diagnostics_result.txt relay@nexus:/logs/diagnostics_result.txt copies it to the relay.

files.home/voyager/ship/control/ship_systems/d:
echo 'Hull: OK'
echo 'Nav: OK'
echo 'Engines: OK' > /home/voyager/ship/control/diagnostics_result.txt

title: Final Countdown
briefing: City defenses have picked up your launch prep and they're closing in. The ignition sequence has to run in exact order, with real timing — not a heartbeat early.
Hold, then go.
objective: Pause for a couple of seconds to let the countdown clear, then confirm ignition by writing GO into ignition.txt.
hints: sleep N pauses for N real seconds before the next command runs.
Chain commands in sequence with a semicolon: sleep 2; echo GO > ignition.txt
The pause has to actually happen before the file is written — order matters here.

title: Escape
briefing: You're off the ground and NEXUS-9 is falling away behind you. One task left: engage the autopilot, then close this session for good.
Congratulations, Commander. Let's go home.
objective: Engage the autopilot, then close out your session.
hints: bash final_systems/autopilot.sh runs the autopilot script directly.
It reports its status to autopilot_status.txt once engaged.
exit (or logout) closes out your terminal session.
